common_name: Rock Candy Pink Penstemon (Compact Early-Flowering Beardtongue)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Rock Candy Pink is part of a compact, first-year-flowering seed series bred for uniform, garden-ready plants.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; good drainage is essential, since penstemon is prone to crown rot in wet, heavy soil. Rock Candy Pink bears upright spikes of clear pink, tubular flowers on a compact plant bred from seed for a uniform, first-year-flowering habit, considerably shorter than many older Penstemon barbatus selections and well suited to the front of a border or a container. Hummingbirds and bees visit the flowers readily, and the plant tolerates heat and drought well once established. Deadhead spent flower spikes to encourage additional bloom, and avoid overly rich soil or excess fertilizer, which causes weak, floppy growth in penstemon.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Firebird bears vivid red-orange tubular flowers that are especially attractive to hummingbirds.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; good drainage is essential, since penstemon is prone to crown rot in wet, heavy soil. Firebird bears tall spikes of vivid, saturated red-orange, tubular flowers over narrow green foliage, a hot color that draws hummingbirds reliably throughout its long summer bloom season. Its upright habit fits well in the middle of a sunny, dry border or a pollinator planting alongside other xeric perennials. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and needs minimal supplemental water beyond the establishment period. Deadhead spent flower spikes to encourage additional bloom, and avoid rich soil or heavy fertilizer, which produces weak, floppy growth.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Elfin Pink is a compact penstemon well suited to small beds, rock gardens, and the front of a border.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; good drainage is essential, since penstemon is prone to crown rot in wet, heavy soil. Elfin Pink bears compact spikes of soft pink, tubular flowers on a low, tidy plant well suited to a rock garden, border edge, or small bed where taller penstemon cultivars would be out of scale. It draws hummingbirds and bees during its summer bloom season and tolerates heat and drought well once established. Deadhead spent flower spikes to encourage continued bloom, and avoid rich soil or heavy fertilizer, both of which produce weak, floppy growth in penstemon.
